In this section we will look at tidymodels.Tidymodels represents a
complete suite of packages designed to simplify machine learning in R.
We will focus on the following core components:

- `rsample`: split datasets into test / training / validation. Also
  includes tools for cross validation

- `recipes`: define a series of steps to pre-process data `parsnip`:
  easy way to try out lots of different models

- `tune`: optimise model hyperparameters (also `dials` which helps with
  tuning)

- `workflows`: bring together sampling, recipes, models and tuning into
  a single workflow

- `yardstick`: check the performance of models `broom`: extract
  important information from models

- There are also various additional packages, more information can be
  found at <https://www.tidymodels.org/packages/>

The easiest way to load these packages is to just call:

```         
library(tidymodels)
```

# Creating testing and training datasets

In machine learning we need a training dataset and a test dataset. We
build our models with the training data, then see how well it predicts
outcomes in a new, unseen, test dataset.

Ideally, our test dataset would be entirely new. Otherwise, we can split
our main dataset. A 70/30 or 80/20 split would be ideal.

Tidymodels provides the `rsample` package which assists. with this.

Let's look at some options:
https://rsample.tidymodels.org/reference/index.html

This time we will use `initial_split()`. Let's take a closer look:
https://rsample.tidymodels.org/reference/initial_split.html

The important options here are: `data` our initial dataset `prop` A
proportion, e.g. 0.8 for a 80/20 split `strata` Optional. Variable to
stratify by

Let's create a set with a 70/30 proportion and stratfied by.


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
ui_data_split <- rsample::initial_split(ui_synthetic_data, prop = _____, strata = '_____')

ui_data_split

```
:::


We could look at the structure of the split object. It comtains the full
dataset, details of how the split was performed and indexes for the
training and test sets:


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
str(ui_data_split)
```
:::


What if we want to extract just the training or test sets? We can do
that using `training()` or `testing()`. Try. both here:


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
rsample::training(ui_data_split) |> as_tibble()
```
:::


Cross validation:

Split the data into five blocks (1-5) then:

train on 1,2,3 and 5, test on 5 train on 1,2,3,5, test on 4 train on
1,2,4,5, test on 3 train on 1,3,4,5, test on 2 train on 2,3,4,5, test on
1

If we want to do cross validation, we can use rsample again, this time
creating cross-validation folds from the training data only:


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
ui_data_cv_folds <-
	rsample::vfold_cv(
		data = rsample::training(ui_data_split),
		v = 5,
		repeats = 5,
		strata = 'urinary_incontinence_late_deterioration'
	)

ui_data_cv_folds
```
:::


v = number of folds repeats - number of times to repea this strata -
ensure equal proportions of the strata. variable in each fold.

In the example we have 5 sets of 5 folds (so 25 in total)

This creates a 5-fold cross validation set, then repeats the process 5
times. A set like this can be used when tuning more complex models such
as LASSO regression models and random forest models. Various paramters
are systematically tested - performance is estimated from the multiple
cross validation sets.

Ultimately this gives us 25 ROC-AUC scores - from this we can estimate
both ROC-AUC and a confidence interval.

# Recipes - processing data

The `recipes` package gives us a large number of data processing steps
to help prepare data for modelling. First we define the recipe using
`recipe()`. To this obejct we add a number of processing steps using
functions beginning with `step_`.

Then we `prep()` the recipe. This step trains the recipe based on the
training data.

For example: a recipe containing `step_corr()` is passed to prep().
prep() feeds the training data to the recipe. step_corr() removes
correlating variables. The prepared recipe contains a list of variables
to be removed.

`bake()` is used to apply those intructions to a dataset. By default the
training set is used, but that dataset can be replaced by any other
(e.g. a test dataset) by setting the `new_data` argument. The result is
a dataset which has been processed using the pre-trained recipe. In our
example, correlating variables identified in training dataset are
removed from the test dataset.

A full list of step\_ functions can be found at
<https://recipes.tidymodels.org/reference/index.html>.

Let's make a simple recipe to process our dataset.


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
ui_recipe <-
	recipes::recipe(training(ui_data_split), 
									formula = urinary_incontinence_late_deterioration ~ .) |>
	# set Subject_ID as a ID role so we don't try and process it later
	recipes::update_role(Subject_ID, new_role = 'id') |>
	# dummy-code all categorical variables
	recipes::step_dummy(all_factor_predictors()) |>
	# remove perdictors with near-zero variance
	recipes::step_nzv(all_predictors()) 
	
ui_recipe_trained <-
	ui_recipe |>
	recipes::prep()
	
ui_recipe_trained
```
:::


If we want to see what happened in each step we can use `tidy()`


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
ui_recipe_trained |> tidy()
```
:::


And to see what was removed in step 2:


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
ui_recipe_trained |> tidy(2)
```
:::


When we call `ui_recipe_trained` we can see that the recipes has:

Identified outcome, predictor and ID variables

Created dummy variables for `p3radio_type`

Removed variables with very little variance:

```         
# A tibble: 8 × 2
  terms                      id       
  <chr>                      <chr>    
1 p3brachy                   nzv_tBNwl
2 ra                         nzv_tBNwl
3 sildenafil                 nzv_tBNwl
4 5alpha_reductase_inhibitor nzv_tBNwl
5 anti_muscarinic            nzv_tBNwl
6 amiodarone                 nzv_tBNwl
7 hip_replacement            nzv_tBNwl
8 SNP4                       nzv_tBNwl

```

We can output a processed training set by setting `new_data` to `NULL`
when calling `bake()`


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
ui_recipe_trained |>
  recipes::bake(new_data = NULL) |>
  as_tibble()
```
:::


Or the test set by setting `new_data` to `test(ui_data_split)`


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
ui_recipe_trained |>
  recipes::bake(new_data = rsample::test(ui_data_test)) |>
  as_tibble()
```
:::
